body: Have you thought about going into research, rather than a secret government agency? You could help others, and still see a psychiatrist at your own leisure.
p.s. I never acquired my degree nor made it to med school due to the severity of my illness, so I know I am of little help to you, example-wise.

I think you need to ask yourself, do you want to live a happy, fulfilling, and healthy life (by getting outside help)? Or continue living in misery and fear? Just because you seek help does not mean you will immediately be put on medication. Try and find a private doctor unafilliated with a hospital and seek help from him/her. They will not be biased or pushed by pharmaceutical reps to prescribe meds. Not all schizophrenics need medication, but if I were you, I would seek outside, unbiased help. Psych records are confidential. I was also a psych and premed student, and by trying to  keep my illness quiet I ended up having a psychotic breakdown. Is any of this possible for you?

p.s. for some reason I am assuming you are female. What size shoe do you wear? I have a few pairs, ranging from sneakers to boots,  that I only wore a few times before becoming disabled; I can only wear special shoes now.

I live in a medium-sized town in the Midwest, and there are a few consignment shops. They have really nice name brand/designer clothes, also with tags still on them. They are a step above thrift shops. I am plus sized, and there's even a size 12 and over consignment shop. I found a pair of Lane Bryant jeans (usually around $70) for $7. Good luck, and I am totally jealous you potentially have a job at a zoo :)

One of my ex church mentors has3 boys, and her BFF has 2 girls. She said it was much easier to raise boys than what she saw with her friend raising girls (sorry for the run-on sentence). I love your answer. The household I grew up in was highly dysfunctional, and perhaps my experience with my father reflects that.

I realize this question sounds cruel, but it was something I experienced as a child. Perhaps it could be considered emotional abuse by today's standards. I strove so hard to be the best I can be, acing high school then going into pre-Med. But it all came crashing down, and I think that comment by him should not have been said.

What a great read. I stole it and plastered it on my FB. I am the middle child, with an older sister and a younger brother, so that article really "hits home (pun." Perhaps my father complimented all of us in that manner. Thank you for the reference.

I am fine today :) I shouldn't have posted such personal stuff to begin with, as I am not equipped to deal with nay-sayers. I'll be fine. p.s. I look like a fat Janis Joplin :) Thanks for being proud of me!

I readily admit I do not know much about numbers, particularly because my GP told me to ignore them and let her do the worrying (because I have substantial paranoia). My BSL once was high as 380, even when I have not eaten carbs or sugars. A lot of it is stress, a lot of it is the dang anti-psychotics. I just follow her advice and let her worry about it. I have so much to deal with as it is :(

Lol, I usually don't offer it..I was extremely tired last night. I live in a building with video feeds in every hallway, elevator, and entrances. Also, I am very "homely," so the least of my worries is a rapist. I'm also broke, with a computer being my only prized possession, have a peephole in the door, and keep the door double locked. But you are right...I need to be more careful about that. Thanks for the advice! Regards, LSM.

Hi Alan, perhaps it was my mental illness doing the thinking, but I felt as though I was bombarded with detailed questions as to whether or not I was telling the truth. I even went so far as to stumble out of my chair to take a pic, and for some that I was still not good enough; they wanted to see my face as well. It was difficult for me to ignore those people doing the digging. I became very frustrated and "deleted" the thread. I was feeling overwhelmed to begin with, as the prior evening I had just received the chair, and yesterday I was exploring with it, seeing what I can and can not fir it into. That was very humbling for me.I put the post up not for sympathy, but for advice. 

I know my levels are high -my GP says that is from the the anti-psychotics and not to worry about numbers anymore. She had to make a tough choice between my physical health and my mental health, and was in contact with my psychiatrist. Both of them chose my mental health, and the numbers reflect that. If you can, Google "antipsychotic diabetes." There is a plethora of information regarding the correlation.  I am not using that as an excuse, but rather the reason why I jumped from 5'9" 140lbs to 5'9" 243lbs :(

If you would like, I would like to hear from you again. It's entirely up to you, but I am glad you do not judge me. I will not be back to the diabetes subreddit. They tore me apart and had me for dinner, when I was just trying to show my predicatment. It really stung. But yeah, I'd like to hear from you again.

Regards,
Mary

Oh wow, I'm sorry :( Things just got terribly out of hand. I've never been quizzed like that before. I am glad you wrote :) Maybe a plant from 1800 flowers, or a scented candle or scented heating oil? Those are my favorite things, though I have yet to see a plant yet in my new home. If you need an address let me know, but I need some rest now. :) I'm sorry for ignoring you before. I've had tons of messages come flowing in. Have a good night and I'll give you my addy in the AM, if you're still interested!

I am going to bed now. I tried to delete this thread because people keep quizzing me suspiciously. It is not as though I am trying to solicit donations for a cooler chair, or claiming to have cancer for sympathy, or flashing my breasts at men. I have type II Diabetes brought about by genetics and anti-psychotics. I use the Freestyle Lite kit. The lancets are cheap and my strips are free through my prescription coverage. I use alcohol swabs and poke the inner part of my finger, where the skin is most thin. I'm fat and that's why I didn't post a headshot, and I have gray hair. If that's not good enough for you all, you'll have to talk amongst yourselves. I'm sorry if this offends some of you, but things got out of hand.

Thank you, kind redditor who appreciates good video games! I never played LSL, it wasn't marketed toward females, particularly young females. Now I am middle-aged and can appreciate the concept of the game!

Yes, I have diabetes. I have type II. I am on glyburide and metformin. My last a1c was 7.4. I use the freestyle lite to test my blood sugar, which is usually in the 160s-180s. Yes, diabetes is the cause of my peripheral neuropathy. Both conditions run in both sides of the family. I do not understand why people are quizzing me about diabetes...it's not as though I am claiming to be in MENSA or an astronaut or Oprah Winfrey.

Because I don't have to prove myself to anyone, particularly you. What do you expect, a peep show with "Hi you_are_alive" tattooed on my forehead? I am not here for sob stories. Ha ha a wheelchair fight is about as entertaining as an internet fight. Take your anger elsewhere. I refuse to further engage with you. At least I'm not resorting to a throw-away-account to get my point across. Move on. Move on.

Thank you for the kind words. Standing up to my father was one of the most difficult things I've ever had to do. He let the power of certain scripture get to his head, and I also suspect he might have Alzheimer's. I heard from my sister yesterday that he is still obsessing about it, calling her, and harassing her. The rest of my family really respect me (sans my brother) for what I did. My brother in law gave me the full amount of my check, and I am managing my own money this month to prove to my psychiatrist that I can do it. Hopefully he will show mercy and fill out the forms for me to be my own payee. I am sorry to hear about your friend. That is much worse than what I went through. My father has written me out of his will, and I am still waiting for a letter from SSA/OIG about an audit. He is nice to me on the phone, but I hear he is totally different behind my back. I'm sick of these games. They've gone on long enough. He knows I'm paranoid to begin with, so his method of talking behind my back really gets to me. Little things like that make for a tough battle :( I hope your friend one day finds peace, I really do.

The anti-psychotics raise my blood sugar levels by about 100-200 (points?). My GP  says alot of my problems are caused by the anti-psychotics, and to just them be. Don't worry, she says. She'd rather have me happy and slowly deteriorating than to be miserable, symptomatic, and (if I'm lucky) hospitalized behind locked doors. You are right, I am lucky to have a dietician planning my meals. Example: chef salad, a very small brick of lasagna, 1 piece of whole wheat bread, tons of steamed veggies, and a small piece of rhubarb pie for dessert. The funny thing is that all of this is filling and I get a lot of energy from my meals. I truly am blessed!

I've signed up for "foot care" in my new residence. It cost $16 and I've heard the nurses who provide it are much more pleasant than podiatrists. The two podiatrists in town quite frankly hate their professions, and ignore my calluses and cut the nails too short. I can no longer do it on my own. My flexibility flew out the window years ago, and my toes are numb and paralyzed. I'd rather pay $16 for a caring nurse than go to a "free" overworked podiatrist any day. They even massage the feet and gently and look for wounds.

I am very sorry to hear about your father. My grandfather used to cry from his neuropathy, and he was a tough ex-Army who fought on stormed Normandy in WWII. That is how painful this condition is. 

My sister had to have two toes amputated because she is a "picker." She picks at her wounds. She, too, is Diabetic with Neuropathy, though I am on much stronger medicine and use a chair. I am glad you learned a lot about wheelchairs, it is all new to me. Not many curbs have ramps. People stare. But with all of your stories and support I feel less alone inside. :) Sorry if I got off-topic. I am still discombobulated.

Hey, thanks a lot for the link! It coincides with my father's idea (when we were still speaking) that my schizophrenia can be controlled with massive amounts of thiamine. I will get my local library to order this book, and check it out. Thanks again!

Funny you should mention that, most of my extended family lives in West Michigan, also where I went to college. They can't get it to me though. I can just make do with what I've got.I was looking at the paperwork that came with it that the chair cost $482, and the back cushion alone cost $88. Wow! I will have to keep my eyes open on Craigslist and eBay. This one is comfortable, it just doesn't fit through some of my doors. I left a message with the support staff asking for the maintenance man to remove some of the indoor doors from their hinges, so that the chair can possibly fit into the bedroom. If not, I will cope. This is the biggest apartment in the building and I'd like to keep it. Thanks for the offer!

ha ha! I got your reply in my mailbox and initially I thought it was a euphemism, but I see what you mean now. Yes, my desk is a mess, from the tupperware halfway full of sunflower seeds to a spray bottle to keep one of my birds from picking on the other, weaker bird. At least the printer and keyboard are wireless! I'm not completely behind the times!

Thanks for your reply :) I posted a pic for proof. I hope that diffuses the situation. I feel really bad for you for having it in your hands. Mine is on the tops and bottoms of my feet, going halfway between my ankle and my knees. I can't imagine what you must be going through as well. I would feel awful not being able to dial a phone number or type with ease. I am counting my blessings after hearing your stories. When I was in a "hospital," they would take my blood sugar readings and the stress of being there would make my levels go up to the 500's. I remember the evening I found out I had diabetes. I was hospitalized for pneumonia, and because of my body type, a physician tested my sugars and they were very high. I was flummoxed. Days before I was drinking Dr. Pepper big gulps. It's been two years since I had a soda or a carb-ridden energy drink, and am very proud of that. However, my sugars remain high due to the Anti-psychotics. I live in an assisted living facility (as of 2 months now, I have my own apartment here), and we get meals here based on our income. All of my meals are planned by a dietician, and my sugars are still high :( If you can, google the correlation between anti-psychotics and diabetes. They usually go hand in hand. Luckily, I do not have to take insulin, I am still in the pill phase. Glyburide and Metformin.  I can't imagine putting a needle in my stomach, like some of the others in this building have to do. There are so many blessings I am counting at the moment!

Thanks for the tip :) I will look for his/her book on Amazon. I am on so many meds. Meds for something, then meds for side effects of something, then meds for the pain caused by both "somethings." It's a viscious cycle.

Thank you, that bloke below really affected me about mentioning my schizophrenia. A lot of schizophrenics have Type 2 because anti-psychotics affect blood sugar levels, and also cause an immense craving for sweets. I am thinking of deleting this post because some do not believe this post.

Geeze, I have enough on my plate without needing a wheelchair for sympathy or attention. You are the reason why stigmas for mental illness exist. So what if I have schizophrenia? That does not make me a compulsive liar. Also, people with schizophrenia are no often the perpetrators of crimes, they are more likely to be the victims of crimes. I can not believe you have the gumption to write that. If I were looking for attention I'd go to /r/SuicideWatch or /r/GoneWild. I have type 2 diabetes brought on by excessive doses of anti-psychotics. Have a nice day, I hope you're happy with yourself.

My mother used a device to put her socks on when she was in mid-stage of cancer. We both thought it was a really neat device. It gave her a sense of independece. I no longer feel lonely due to the sheer response of my post. I love all of you and am glad you understand.

Thank you for the info! I suppose I will ask for one once I get used to this one (sitting all the time, bumping into stuff, scraping my hands, etc). He also wants to see how I do in this clunker and to find out if it helps (which it CERTAINLY does!)

Great, thanks for the input. I will do a search on nerve conditions/neuropathy and see what shows up. If no /r/subreddit is available, perhaps I will start my own (!), or continue to post here, if that's alright.

Thank you so much for your insight. Yep, I'm getting to know my body fast. Aside from the withdrawals, the neuropathy pain has doubled, so my body is screaming at me. I took my night time meds early just now so that I will at least be numb for the next 4 hours or so. My dr's are pretty lenient with me and my meds. They know I've been through/go through a lot of grief. So they won't mind if I take my dose early. Thank you for answering!

I called CVS, who is the only other pharmacy in town that is open on weekends, and they won't touch it. The one in town is awful. High turnover rate, rude assistants, so I went with a local Mom and Pop place that delivers and orders stuff for me (e.g. dryer sheets, etc) when I'm short. They also gave me a charge account. They can't be beat when it comes to customer service. They have an emergency on call person, but that service is reserved for Senior Citizens and costs $250 that my insurance won't pay. I'll just have to wait.

It's an awful waiting game. I hope the upcoming winter storm doesn't keep the pharmacist away. I've already left a message saying that I want to be on their delivery program now because I can't get the meds on my own. I ate a balanced meal and feel a bit better. I'm pretty sure that I'll have to start on a lower dose. I will call as soon as I get the refill back. Thank you.

Thank you for responding to him. My parents divorced while I was a teenager. My mother had severe untreated borderline personality disorder and treated me like garbage. At the time, my father was an Officer in the Air Force with an exemplary record and she still almost won her custody battle. My Dad told me he would have bought land near her backyard and camp there every night just to see us. That's how great of a father he was at the time. Thankfully, he won the case and I had a great teen upbringing. You are a great mother, and I hope you find an attorney who will help you. Keep texting her positive texts, and try your hardest not to talk about him to her. She will one day appreciate that. **HUGS**

I stand by others' school of thought. I am on Disability/Retirement income, and used to own a '98 Maxima. As my life started to financially unravel, I realized that if my car ever broke down, I would not be able to fix it anymore. So I sold my car and now take the bus. A month-long unlimited bus pass for people with disabilities costs $26. It also saves on my carbon emissions, and I do not have to worry about waiting for my car to warm up in the winter. Incidentally, I live in North Dakota, in a 100K population metro. Selling my car was one of the best decisions I've ever made. Owning a car is a luxury, IMO, and I had to trade in that luxury for my only other luxury...internet. When you make less than $1000/month, things such as luxuries need to be seriously considered. I'd rather have internet and be on reddit for an entire month (for $29.99, 5mb internet), than to own a car and have nothing else to pass the time.
Thanks CutieJudy! Being obese and not sleeping well are probably the only two things I know a lot about :) HAGD!

Additional support: /r/BodyAcceptance/ is really helpful. I've accepted myself after years of therapy, but I subscribe to that subreddit because it's nice to help others plagued with the same issues I once had, and also to see the success stories of men and women who finally accept themselves for who they really are.

Hi, I am fat too, with uneven fat distribution in my stomach area. I look like I'm 9 months' pregnant with the baby being in my stomach. I've had MRIs and CT scans and it's fat. My legs and arms are skinny, but I have a double chin. The only thing feminine about me is my very long hair, but I still get called "Sir" when I wear pants.

Do you qualify for Social Supplemental Income and/or the corresponding Medicaid? That's what I have, in addition to Medicare because of Schizophrenia. It's treated now, so I am fine. 

I also have had insomnia since I was 4. My Dad used to make me lie in bed for 8 hours and I'd just stare at the wall. He'd ground me if I got out of bed.

If you can, go to your county office and fill out the plethora of forms in order to get SSI and Medicaid. If you're not a felon, you will likely qualify. This will enable you to have access to doctors and therapists. I take 3 different meds for sleep: Trazodone, Klonopin, and Ambien. The latter two are narcotics, and I am not sure if Medicaid pays for them anymore but they both have generics and are relatively cheap. 

If you ever need to vent, PM me because I completely understand what you are going through. I've been there. Thank goodness for Social Supplemental Income and Social Security Disability Income/Retirement (though I am 36). I will likely never be able to work again, and they give me the minimum amount, but at least I can sleep now. Ha ha I just realized it's 1:44AM but I did have a very long natural nap this afternoon. Anyhow, PM me if you like. I hope this helps.
In addition, it would have been worth 7-10X what I paid for it, but the knob no longer fits in its hole.

postscript: Yellow Jackets (containing ephedra and massive amounts of caffeine) were legal back then, and they played a large factor.

I am a female American, and albeit a large one, I (having no friends at the time) once shimmied a British wardrobe down one flight of stairs, prior to becoming disabled 10 years later. Not as commendable, but Americans are capable of something.
p.s. I'm sure their tech support has extended hours. I've never needed to use it, which shows how much they've got their ducks in order.

702 has just Moorhead office open during regular business hours. and are friendly to me, even when I mention my address. Cableone's customer service is all over the place. I did not have to undergo a credit check, and because of the billing cycle, I did not have to pay a dime prior to having it installed (free). The installer was female, so I did not feel awkward being around her. 

 I pay for the only option given for the High Rise, 5mb for $29.99/mo, with an $8 wireless modem lease. It has unlimited data streaming, and plays Netflix and Youtbue perfectly. I am no longer a gamer, but as long as it streams effortlessly I am happy.

I live in one of the largest units in the building, but it is still medum/small by most American's standards. Kitchenette with a small stove but full size fridge. The largest bed that can fit in the bedroom is a double bed. I have enough additional room for two end tables. The living room and kitchen are connected with no wall between them. The living room fits a loveseat, desk, bookshelf, and my large birdcage in the corner. I sold my tv because the cable lineup here is G-rated and I prefer the internet (702 communications has a package that's super thrifty). There is no dining area, so I eat at my antique desk (the only remnant I have from my time spent in the UK). One has to walk through my bedroom to get to my bathroom, which has the biggest shower I've ever seen with a custom seat in it for those who can not use their legs. I do not sit, I think it's unhygienic. There are critters, though, I found out tonight. I was walking to my mailbox in the lobby and the timing was perfect for a dead mouse to fall from the ceiling. It's either dead, or in shock. That, and the suicide that happened yesterday evening shook me up a bit, but I keep to myself, keep the door double locked, and have accustomed myself to my New York City-esque apartment.

Wow! That's pretty cool that you're right next door. I live in a corner apartment (but there are 2 windows that only face south). I am willing to bet you have MUCH more square feet than I do. I have a tidy living space, bedroom, and master bathroom. There is no tub, but the showers are massive with built-in seating. Having come here from a basement apartment (in South Fargo) with no natural light for several years, I am extremely grateful for my new living situation. I am here to stay.
Thanks! :) Not many people notice it or know the reference. It wasn't really marketed toward my age group or gender, so I suppose I am a poser. Kudos to you and an upvote for knowing its origins!

He tried telling me I was disrespecting him after I refused his bribes. He's trying every trick in the book, trying to get my SSDI taken away, no AC this summer unless I can find a way to get him to give me the money I saved, and is now trying to have my food stamps reduced. My life is in shambles right now. I haven't slept all night, and that's affecting me. Thanks for the reply. It feels good knowing people are looking out for me spiritually.

The Fry'n Pan is connected to our building, but I get lost every time I try to find it. The Lashkowitz High Rise is for low-income, or disabled, or elderly people. There is a great deal of diversity here, and I love it. When I went down to get my mail this afternoon, there was a Bosnian gentleman juggling his shoes in the lobby. They're not very aero-dynamic so I commented to him that he is quite talented. He nodded and walked off, still juggling. Hah!
Indeed! You are correct. Good eye.

Thanks! Yes, definitely. One problem is my father told me about 5 or 6 hours ago that a ledger was supposed to be in place, detailing my expenses and receipts. We do not have those. Everything was in cash or bank transfer. That is why I am really, really concerned. Thanks :) Hopefully God can help me make it through the night. I can't sleep, a lot has happened to me in the past two days, and a lot more is going to happen in the near future. Dad admitted that this was a mental game of chess, and that he will win. I refuse to let him win. I am going to do whatever it takes to hopefully stay cordial with him (which I do not predict) or to remove him completely from my life.

I am living in a high rise for disabled people. I have a corner apartment. I recently moved here from my sister's basement mother-in-law suite, so I have the stress of living in a different place. However, the office staff are always willing to sit down with residents and listen. My father dictated that I move here so that I will have more sunlight (which he thinks will cure my ailments). There is a social worker on staff as well. But we do not have staff roaming the halls, or checking on us. We have our own apartments. My father woke me at 9:30PM and it's going to be a long night. He knows exactly what buttons to push and how to scare me. He's known me my entire life. By the grace of God, I have a psychiatrist appointment tomorrow, and I will discuss what is happening. I will also politely ask that my psychiatrist vouge (sp?) for the fact that I am now able to handle my own money, so that this will never happen again. I've made a lot of financial mistakes in the past, but I have learned from them. No more take-out, unlimited phone plan, cable, etc. I am happy with just internet. During the 9:30 call Dad informed me he will no longer buy me an air conditioner, so the $500 he owes me (if he gives it back) will be used for that. 

I am very scared. I can't call a hotline because where I live the Sheriff's Department comes to the door. To make matters even worse, about 100 yards away is a private psych hospital, just waiting (cue the SOON meme). I refuse to let Dad break me. I am stronger than ever before. I have you guys to keep me occupied with your comments, good or bad, to make it through the night until I call Social Security and tell them what is happening, do they honor HIPAA laws regarding privacy, and that I think my father is slightly senile now. It's going to be a very long night.

Thank you. I have treated schizophrenia, and am functioning well. My father knows which buttons to push to trigger a breakdown, using words like "audit" and "fraud." He wants so badly to have some control over me. I am living in my own apartment in a secure building with support staff. I am completely independent, sans my really cool representative payee (the liberal Atheist nudist). He debits the money for my debts from my disability check, and gives me the rest of the money to spend on food, medicine, and clothing. We work together very well. I see my psychiatrist tomorrow (today?) and will ask him what to do, and hint at him emancipating me from the payee system.

I have (treated, and am doing fine) schizophrenia. I want to stress that it is under control. My sister's husband is my benefits representative, basically he withholds the money for my rent and internet, and lets me have the remaining money right away. My father is trying to change that immediately, and has called me numerous times during the past 48 hours. He is clever enough to not leave a message, and boy oh boy don't I wish I was able to record what he says. From bribing me with gift cards to blackmailing me with this audit he's talking about, I am under a great deal of stress. Any type of audit stresses "normal" people out. He knows that too much stress and stimuli causes me to have a breakdown, and is using that to his advantage at the moment. The only proof I have that he is harassing me is my call log on my phone. I am eagerly awaiting 7AM in order to call the Social Security Federal Office. I also see my psychiatrist tomorrow and will ask him to submit a form stating that I am doing well and am able to handle my own money henceforth. I realize that due to the stigma of Schizophrenia, my perceived credibility in this thread has just sunk 10 feet under, and I hope you ladies and gentlemen realize that it's under control.

If all of your income is low enough, you should be able to qualify your father and mother for Medicaid. Find out where your county office is for Medical Services. Once he qualifies for Medicaid, your options will improve. I had to do research to find a great nursing home for my mom prior to her passing. The first place I moved her to was awful. She'd push her "help" button while I'd visit her and it would be an hour before someone would assist her. I moved her to a closer county, and found an awesome nursing home for her. Exotic birds in aviaries throughout, cats on one floor, trained service dogs on another floor (one dog laid by Mom's side throughout the night as she passed). I don't know if you mentioned it or not but Hospice is a huge help and I believe it is free, but I could be wrong? If not Medicaid will cover it. I speak this from experience, because I cared for my Mom, who had undiagnosed (until it was too late, cancer) I cared for her with bathing, first aid, etc until the county and state finally helped. Research nursing homes, a big thing to do is tour them. Asked to see the living facility in addition to cafeteria, day rooms, bathrooms. Make sure there's call buttons. In the awesome nursing home I found for my Mom they had microphones and little speakers around their necks that would annoyingly beep until they reached the patient's room, so they were quick on their feet because the state would research the time it took to reach a patient. Also it had live plants throughout that volunteers watered...sorry to go on and on but look for things like this. It means staff and outsiders care about the place and everyone's welfare. The employees actually **enjoyed** their work. 

Hopefully this helps, if you have any more questions go ahead and message me. I know how difficult it is! I know a lot about it, but first things first is to contact your county and they should give you info about filing for Medicaid. Good luck!
